questions.q: A CSV is loaded and order_date has dtype object. What is the standard way to convert it to real dates?
questions.explain: pd.to_datetime parses text into datetime64 values. You can also do this while loading with read_csv(parse_dates=[...]).

questions.q: What does errors="coerce" do in pd.to_datetime?
options: Turns values that cannot be parsed into NaT instead of raising an error
Deletes the rows that cannot be parsed
Forces every value to today's date
Rounds every date to the nearest month
questions.explain: Unparseable values become NaT (not a time). You should then count them to see how much data failed to parse.

questions.q: Why is passing an explicit format= to pd.to_datetime recommended for production code?
options: It makes parsing produce time zones
It removes guessing about ambiguous strings such as 03/04/2024
It stores dates as text, which is smaller
It is the only way to parse dates
questions.explain: An explicit format tells pandas exactly which part is the day and which is the month, so ambiguous dates are never silently misread.

questions.q: Which expression gives the number of days between an analysis date `snap` and each order date?
questions.explain: Subtracting dates gives a Timedelta Series, and .dt.days converts it to whole days.

questions.q: In pandas, what does dt.dayofweek return for a Monday?
questions.explain: dayofweek counts Monday as 0 through Sunday as 6. Use dt.day_name() for the text name.
